newsitem.title: INDIA: India state sugar prices need to be hiked - agency.
newsitem.headline: India state sugar prices need to be hiked - agency.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra was quoted as saying on Tuesday that India would have to bear an additional subsidy burden of 7.2 billion rupees if state-controlled sugar prices were not raised by 1.60 rupees per kg.
The choice was to "... raise the price by 1.60 rupees a kilo or be prepared to slap another subsidy of 7.2 billion rupees on the exchequer," the United News of India (UNI) quoted Mishra as saying.
Mishra said the "... proposed hike of 1.60 rupees a kilo, yet to be approved by the cabinet, was only meant to offset the increase in production costs of levy sugar."
An Indian newspaper said on Tuesday the cabinet's decision on raising the levy on sugar prices was expected on Wednesday but it was not immediately clear if the hike would be passed on to consumers.
Sugar supplies and pricing in India are controlled by the government.
Millers supply 40 percent of their output to the government at below the market rates for distribution through government shops at subsidised prices.
